instructions: The night before, put the 8 oz dried chickpeas in a large bowl and cover them with cold water by at least 3 inches. Leave them on the counter overnight. They'll more than double in size.
The next day, drain the chickpeas in a colander and shake them as dry as you can. Don't swap in canned chickpeas. Cooked ones are too wet, and the falafel fall apart in the oil.
Roughly chop 1 cup of leaves from the parsley and 1 cup of leaves from the cilantro. Finely chop the white and light green parts of the green onions, and mince 2 of the garlic cloves.
Put the chickpeas, herbs, green onions and minced garlic in a food processor. Add the 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp coriander, 1 1/2 tsp of the salt, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 4 tsp flour and 5 tbsp water.
Blend on high for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping down the sides a couple of times, until the chickpeas are tiny grains and the green mix holds together when you squeeze a little in your hand.
Scoop up heaped tablespoons and roll them into balls about 1 inch wide. Set them on a plate. You should get about 20.
Put the plate in the fridge for 30 minutes. Chilled falafel hold together better in the oil.
Meanwhile, make the tahini sauce. Grate the last garlic clove into a bowl, add the 1/4 cup tahini and 2 tbsp juice squeezed from the lemon, and stir. It will turn thick and stiff.
Stir in 4 tbsp water, 1 tbsp at a time, until it's loose enough to drizzle. Stir in the last 1/4 tsp salt.
Slice the 2 tomatoes and the 2 cucumbers into thin rounds. Slice a few of the pickles.

Pour the 2 cups vegetable oil into a heavy medium pot so it's at least 3/4 inch deep, and heat it over medium high. You're heating it to about 355°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it. No thermometer? Drop in a pinch of the mix. It's ready when it sizzles hard right away.

Slide in 6 or 7 falafel with a spoon, leaving room between them. Stand back a little. The oil can spatter. Fry for about 4 minutes, rolling them with two forks, until they're deep golden brown and crusty all over.
Lift them onto paper towels with a slotted spoon. Fry the rest the same way in 2 more batches.
Warm 4 of the pitas in a dry skillet over medium for about 30 seconds, then flip them and warm the other side for 30 seconds, until soft.
Lay 5 falafel down the middle of each pita and press them lightly to break them open. Add the tomato, cucumber and pickles, drizzle with tahini sauce and roll it up.
Serve right away, with the rest of the tahini sauce on the side.
advance_prep_notes: soak the dried chickpeas overnight, the night before
method_notes: All three soak dried chickpeas overnight and grind them raw with herbs, onion, garlic and cumin; none uses canned. RecipeTin Eats blends the chickpeas with parsley, cilantro, green onion, coriander, a little flour, baking powder and water to a fine paste, chills the balls 30 minutes and shallow fries them at about 355°F, serving them in pita with tahini sauce. Zaatar and Zaytoun makes it half dried fava beans, adds baking soda to the soak, seven spice and chilli to the mix, and rolls the balls in sesame seeds before deep frying. The Matbakh uses onion and allspice and folds the baking powder in after an hour in the fridge. This one follows RecipeTin Eats with chickpeas only.
